facts.text: Olney was originally called Mechanicsville, founded in 1800 at the crossroads of the Rockville‑to‑Baltimore road and the Washington‑Westminster road.
The town’s name comes from the Olney House, built in 1800 and named after Olney, England, where the founding Farquhar family were fans of poet William Cowper.
Olney Theatre, founded in 1938 as a playhouse, became one of Maryland’s two state theaters and was integrated long before 1948 when Helen Hayes staged a play there.
In 1951, Olney hosted the original headquarters of the Emergency Management Institute, the Civil Defense Staff College that trained civil defense personnel nationwide.
The historic Sandy Spring Museum, once a stop on the Underground Railroad, showcases blacksmiths, carpenters, and merchants that once served the early village.
Olney’s economy relied on a blacksmith, a wheelwright shop, Canby’s pottery factory, and Benedict Duley’s general store, all located at the intersection that defines the town’s center today.
